at.name: Austria
at.law: Netz- und Informationssystemsicherheitsgesetz 2026 (NISG 2026), BGBl. I Nr. 94/2025, in force on 1 October 2026. Initial registration is due by 1 January 2027.
at.authority: Bundesamt für Cybersicherheit, a new federal office under the Bundesministerium für Inneres
at.csirt: CERT.at / GovCERT Austria; significant incidents are reported through the NIS2 Services application in the Unternehmensserviceportal (USP)

be.name: Belgium
be.law: Loi/Wet of 26 April 2024 transposing NIS2, in force 18 October 2024, one of the first in the EU. Registration was due by 18 March 2025. Essential entities had a first conformity assessment due by 18 April 2026 and need CyberFundamentals or ISO 27001 certification by 18 April 2027.

bg.name: Bulgaria
bg.law: Act amending the Cybersecurity Act (Закон за киберсигурност), adopted on 5 February 2026, published in the State Gazette on 13 February 2026 and in force since 17 February 2026
bg.authority: Ministry of e-Government, which keeps the central register of entities, and sector competent authorities designated by the Council of Ministers
bg.csirt: CERT Bulgaria at govcert.bg, with sectoral CSIRTs

hr.name: Croatia
hr.law: Zakon o kibernetičkoj sigurnosti (Cybersecurity Act), NN 14/2024, in force 15 February 2024; first member state to transpose
hr.authority: Sigurnosno-obavještajna agencija (SOA), the central state authority for cybersecurity
hr.csirt: The CSIRT at SOA or the national CERT at CARNET, depending on the entity; CARNET runs the national reporting platform

cy.name: Cyprus
cy.law: Security of Networks and Information Systems (Amendment) Law of 2025, N. 60(I)/2025, amending Law 89(I)/2020 to transpose NIS2, in force 25 April 2025
cy.authority: Digital Security Authority (DSA / Αρχή Ψηφιακής Ασφάλειας)
cy.note: Cyprus shortens the NIS2 reporting clocks: early warning within 6 hours instead of 24, final report within 15 days of restoring the affected system instead of one month, and progress reports every 15 days while an incident is still open.

reporting.trigger: Significant incident, essential and important entities
reporting.deadline: Early warning ≤ 6 h; notification ≤ 72 h; progress report every 15 days while open; final report ≤ 15 days after restoration
reporting.recipient: Digital Security Authority (DSA), which also hosts CSIRT-CY

cz.name: Czechia
cz.law: Act No. 264/2025 Sb. on Cybersecurity (zákon o kybernetické bezpečnosti), replacing Act 181/2014, in force 1 November 2025
cz.authority: NÚKIB (Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost)
cz.csirt: GovCERT.CZ under NÚKIB, and national CSIRT.CZ

dk.name: Denmark
dk.law: Family of acts in force since 2025: NIS 2-loven (Lov nr. 434/2025), Lov om styrket beredskab i energisektoren (Lov nr. 258/2025), Lov om sikkerhed og beredskab i telesektoren and CER-loven; finance via Lov om finansiel virksomhed
dk.csirt: SAMSIK, Styrelsen for Samfundssikkerhed, is the national CSIRT. Reporting via virk.dk; energy-sector entities report to Energistyrelsen, and to the CSIRT as well when network and information security was compromised
dk.note: NIS2 and CER arrive as a family of acts rather than one law. SAMSIK coordinates across sectors, and sector authorities supervise their own; Energistyrelsen supervises energy, with its own reporting rules under BEK 260. SAMSIK guidance uses skal / bør / kan tiers; map your control evidence to it.

acts.name: NIS 2-loven
acts.desc: Lov nr. 434/2025 — horizontal Danish NIS2 act

acts.name: Lov om styrket beredskab i energisektoren
acts.desc: Lov nr. 258/2025 — energy sector, NIS2 + CER combined, five preparedness levels

acts.name: Lov om sikkerhed og beredskab i telesektoren
Lov om finansiel virksomhed § 333 ff.
acts.desc: Financial sector, aligned with DORA — tick DORA above as well

reporting.trigger: Significant incident, entities under NIS 2-loven or the tele act

reporting.deadline: 24 h / 72 h status / 1 month incident report
reporting.recipient: Energistyrelsen; incidents that compromised network and information security also to the CSIRT, through the channel it designates; electricity, gas and hydrogen entities also alert Energinet (BEK 260 §§ 77–79)

govern.text: Registration duty on virk.dk for covered entities, per NIS 2-loven § 33.
Top management approves the preparedness plans and is accountable for them; at levels 4 and 5 the preparedness and cyber coordinator must be separate from the management that approves them.

protect.text: Every entity segments its supply-critical systems behind a DMZ or equivalent; levels 4 and 5 separate those networks physically (BEK 260 § 62).

detect.text: Levels 4 and 5 log and monitor to identify incidents in real time, respond in real time, keep logs for 13 months and hand them to their IT security service within 24 h (BEK 260 §§ 66–69).

respond.text: Report via virk.dk; drill the flow against the 24 h early-warning clock.

Report significant incidents to Energistyrelsen within 24 h, with status within 72 h and a report within one month. Exercise the preparedness plans yearly at levels 3 to 5 and every second year at level 2, with a yearly recovery exercise of supply-critical systems at levels 4 and 5 (BEK 260 §§ 21, 77–78).

dk.disclaimer: Community-maintained orientation, the reference annex for the framework. This is **not legal advice**; verify against retsinformation.dk and samsik.dk before relying on it. Corrections welcome, see [contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md).

ee.name: Estonia
ee.law: Act amending the Cybersecurity Act (küberturvalisuse seadus), adopted on 10 December 2025, RT I, 30.12.2025, 4, in force 1 January 2026. Entities register with RIA from 1 April 2026; governance obligations apply from 1 January 2027 and technical requirements from 1 January 2028.
ee.authority: Riigi Infosüsteemi Amet (RIA, Information System Authority)

fi.name: Finland
fi.law: Kyberturvallisuuslaki (Cybersecurity Act 124/2025), in force 8 April 2025. Registration was due by 8 May 2025 and the risk-management operating model by 8 July 2025.
fi.authority: Sector supervisory authorities, including Traficom, the Energy Authority, Tukes, Valvira and Fimea; Traficom's NCSC-FI coordinates them and is the single point of contact

fr.name: France
fr.law: Projet de loi relatif à la résilience des infrastructures critiques et au renforcement de la cybersécurité, transposing NIS2, CER and DORA adjustments. Adopted by the Senate on 12 March 2025; it was due in the Assemblée nationale in October 2026 but was withdrawn from the agenda on 6 October 2026, and no new date has been set. The European Commission referred the country to the Court of Justice of the EU on 9 July 2026 for failing to transpose NIS2.
fr.authority: ANSSI (Agence nationale de la sécurité des systèmes d'information)

de.name: Germany
de.law: NIS-2-Umsetzungs- und Cybersicherheitsstärkungsgesetz (NIS2UmsuCG), amending the BSIG, in force 6 December 2025 with no transition period
de.authority: BSI (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik)

gr.name: Greece
gr.law: Law 5160/2024 transposing NIS2, in force since late November 2024
gr.authority: National Cybersecurity Authority (Εθνική Αρχή Κυβερνοασφάλειας), also the single point of contact
gr.csirt: The national CSIRT, hosted by the National Cybersecurity Authority

hu.name: Hungary
hu.law: Act LXIX of 2024 on Hungary's cybersecurity, in force 1 January 2025 and amended with effect from 31 May 2025

ie.name: Ireland
ie.law: National Cyber Security Bill. The General Scheme was published in 2024, but the bill itself had not been published as of early October 2026; it is a priority on the government's autumn 2026 legislative programme. The European Commission referred the country to the Court of Justice of the EU on 9 July 2026 for failing to transpose NIS2.
ie.authority: Expected: NCSC Ireland as lead competent authority, plus sector regulators

it.name: Italy
it.law: Decreto legislativo 4 settembre 2024, n. 138, in force 16 October 2024

lv.name: Latvia
lv.law: Nacionālās kiberdrošības likums (National Cybersecurity Law), in force 1 September 2024. Entities had to notify the National Cybersecurity Centre by 1 April 2025.
lv.authority: National Cybersecurity Centre under the Ministry of Defence

lt.name: Lithuania
lt.law: Amended Kibernetinio saugumo įstatymas (Cybersecurity Law), applying from 18 October 2024, with implementing rules in force 12 November 2024; among the first transpositions
lt.authority: NKSC (National Cyber Security Centre under MoND)

lu.name: Luxembourg
lu.law: Law of 5 May 2026 on measures for a high common level of cybersecurity, Mémorial A No. 225 of 2026, in force 10 May 2026, replacing the 2019 NIS law
lu.authority: ILR (Institut Luxembourgeois de Régulation) for most sectors; CSSF for the financial sector; HCPN for cyber-crisis management

mt.name: Malta
mt.law: Measures for a High Common Level of Cybersecurity across the European Union (Malta) Order, S.L. 460.41, Legal Notice 71 of 2025, amended by Legal Notice 89 of 2026
mt.authority: Critical Infrastructure Protection Department, competent authority and single point of contact; the Malta Communications Authority for certain digital entities
mt.csirt: The national CSIRT within the Critical Infrastructure Protection Department; confirm the reporting channel

nl.name: Netherlands
nl.law: Cyberbeveiligingswet (Cbw) and Wet weerbaarheid kritieke entiteiten (Wwke, the CER transposition), adopted by the Eerste Kamer on 7 July 2026 and in force since 15 August 2026, with no transition period. Registration with NCSC-NL was due by the same date.
nl.authority: Sector supervisory authorities, with RDI (Rijksinspectie Digitale Infrastructuur) for digital infrastructure
nl.csirt: NCSC-NL; incidents are reported through the national reporting portal to the CSIRT and the competent authority

pl.name: Poland
pl.law: Act amending the Act on the National Cybersecurity System (nowelizacja ustawy o krajowym systemie cyberbezpieczeństwa, KSC), signed on 19 February 2026 and in force since 3 April 2026. Applications to the register of essential and important entities were due by 3 October 2026, the obligations apply from 3 April 2027, and the first audit is due by 3 April 2028.
pl.authority: Ministry of Digital Affairs + sector authorities
pl.csirt: CSIRT NASK, CSIRT GOV and CSIRT MON, a three-CSIRT model

pt.name: Portugal
pt.law: Decreto-Lei n.º 125/2025 of 4 December, the regime jurídico da cibersegurança transposing NIS2, in force 3 April 2026

ro.name: Romania
ro.law: OUG nr. 155/2024, the emergency ordinance transposing NIS2, in force 31 December 2024 and approved with amendments by Law No. 124/2025, in force 10 July 2025. Registration with DNSC under Order 1/2025 was due by 22 September 2025.

sk.name: Slovakia
sk.law: Act No. 366/2024 Z. z. amending Act No. 69/2018 on Cybersecurity, effective 1 January 2025; implementing decrees 226/2025 and 227/2025 apply from 1 September 2025

si.name: Slovenia
si.law: ZInfV-1 (Zakon o informacijski varnosti), the new Information Security Act transposing NIS2, Uradni list RS No. 40/2025 of 4 June 2025, in force 19 June 2025
si.authority: Urad Vlade Republike Slovenije za informacijsko varnost (URSIV), the Government Information Security Office

es.name: Spain
es.status: Pending, bill not yet in parliament
es.law: Anteproyecto de Ley de Coordinación y Gobernanza de la Ciberseguridad, approved in first reading by the Council of Ministers on 14 January 2025 but never sent to the Cortes. The Cortes were dissolved on 5 October 2026 ahead of the general election on 29 November 2026, so the next government has to restart the process. The European Commission referred the country to the Court of Justice of the EU on 9 July 2026 for failing to transpose NIS2.
es.authority: Expected: National Cybersecurity Centre coordination; CCN for the public sector, INCIBE for private entities and citizens, sector authorities

se.name: Sweden
se.law: Cybersäkerhetslag (2025:1506), the Cybersecurity Act transposing NIS2, in force 15 January 2026
se.authority: Myndigheten för civilt försvar, MCF, named MSB until 2026, issues the regulations; sector supervisory authorities supervise
se.csirt: CERT-SE, part of the National Cyber Security Centre at FRA since 1 July 2026
